name: Learn basic travel photography
blurb: Photographs that convey a place rather than just proving you were there: light, timing, people, detail and a sense of story.
gear: A camera you will actually carry
steps: Learn to shoot at the right time: sunrise and the hour after, and the hour before sunset. Midday sun flattens everything.
Learn to include people for scale and story, and to ask permission where appropriate. Learn the local norms about photographing people.
Shoot a variety per location: a wide establishing shot, a medium context shot, and a tight detail. That set tells a story where one wide shot does not.
Learn to avoid the postcard shot by moving — find the angle everyone else is not standing at.
Learn to travel light. A camera left in the hotel takes no photographs.
Back up daily, to a second card or the cloud, and cull ruthlessly each evening.
tips: Ask before photographing people close up. A refused shot costs you nothing; a stolen one can cost a lot.
Check local rules about photographing government buildings, military sites and religious spaces.
proof: A 20-image edit from one trip that tells a coherent story to someone who has never been.
